GRU padding can alter state even with zero padding embeddings: recurrent gates and biases still execute. Thus final-nonpadding readout alone cannot remove effects from preceding left padding. PyTorch supports packed recurrence; first extract each real history and right-pad internally before packing, because packing retains the first `length` positions. Alternatively, explicitly preserve hidden state on padding steps. Keep external histories left-padded and preserve `log2feats`, `item_emb`, and `predict_score`; read the greatest nonzero position, never `count-1`. These implications follow from the documented [GRU equations](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html) and [packing behavior](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html).

Proposed metamorphic suite: freeze the single trained category model, use evaluation/inference mode, and reset hidden state independently for every history. Compare identical real histories with several leading-padding lengths, alone versus mixed-length batches, reordered batches, and individually unpadded execution. Include singleton histories and consecutive calls with unrelated histories to expose state leakage; define empty-history behavior separately. Compare aligned real-token features and final features, then identical candidate scores and ranks. Report maximum absolute error, relative L2 error, top-10 overlap, target-rank change, and score margins around rank 10. Padding-dependent drift suggests recurrent updates; matching token features but differing final features suggests readout/indexing.

Do not require bitwise equality: [PyTorch documents batch-versus-slice numerical differences](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html). Suggested FP32 starting tolerances are `atol=1e-5, rtol=1.3e-6`, matching [assert_close defaults](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/testing). Calibrate against repeated identical executions and batch permutations; rerun suspicious cases without mixed precision/TF32 and optionally in FP64. Treat rank flips within measured score uncertainty as tie-sensitive; persistent errors above that baseline warrant investigation.
